verses.pali: Aṅguttara Nikāya 7.52
verses.english: Numbered Discourses 7.52

verses.pali: 5. Mahāyaññavagga
verses.english: 5. A Great Sacrifice

verses.pali: Dānamahapphalasutta
verses.english: A Very Fruitful Gift

verses.pali: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā campāyaṁ viharati gaggarāya pokkharaṇiyā tīre.
verses.english: At one time the Buddha was staying near Campā on the banks of the Gaggarā Lotus Pond.

verses.pali: Atha kho sambahulā campeyyakā upāsakā yena āyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ sāriputtaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho campeyyakā upāsakā āyasmantaṁ sāriputtaṁ etadavocuṁ:
verses.english: Then several lay followers of Campā went to Venerable Sāriputta, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him,

verses.pali: “cirassutā no, bhante, bhagavato sammukhā dhammīkathā.
verses.english: “Sir, it’s been a long time since we’ve heard a Dhamma talk from the Buddha.

verses.pali: Sādhu mayaṁ, bhante, labheyyāma bhagavato sammukhā dhammiṁ kathaṁ savanāyā”ti.
verses.english: It would be good if we got to hear a Dhamma talk from the Buddha.”

verses.pali: “Tenahāvuso, tadahuposathe āgaccheyyātha,
verses.english: “Well then, reverends, come on the next sabbath day.

verses.pali: appeva nāma labheyyātha bhagavato sammukhā dhammiṁ kathaṁ savanāyā”ti.
verses.english: Hopefully you’ll get to hear a Dhamma talk from the Buddha.”

verses.pali: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho campeyyakā upāsakā āyasmato sāriputtassa paṭissutvā uṭṭhāyāsanā āyasmantaṁ sāriputtaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā pakkamiṁsu.
verses.english: “Yes, sir” they replied. Then they rose from their seats, bowed to Sāriputta, and respectfully circled him before leaving.

verses.pali: Atha kho campeyyakā upāsakā tadahuposathe yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ sāriputtaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhaṁsu.
verses.english: Then on the next sabbath the lay followers of Campā went to Venerable Sāriputta, bowed, and stood to one side.

verses.pali: Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto tehi campeyyakehi upāsakehi saddhiṁ yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā sāriputto bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: Then they went together with Sāriputta to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. Sāriputta said to the Buddha:

verses.pali: “Siyā nu kho, bhante, idhekaccassa tādisaṁyeva dānaṁ dinnaṁ na mahapphalaṁ hoti na mahānisaṁsaṁ;
verses.english: “Sir, could it be that someone gives a gift and it is not very fruitful or beneficial,

verses.pali: siyā pana, bhante, idhekaccassa tādisaṁyeva dānaṁ dinnaṁ mahapphalaṁ hoti mahānisaṁsan”ti?
verses.english: while someone else gives exactly the same gift and it is very fruitful and beneficial?”

verses.pali: “Siyā, sāriputta, idhekaccassa tādisaṁyeva dānaṁ dinnaṁ na mahapphalaṁ hoti na mahānisaṁsaṁ;
verses.english: “Indeed it could, Sāriputta.”

verses.pali: siyā pana, sāriputta, idhekaccassa tādisaṁyeva dānaṁ dinnaṁ mahapphalaṁ hoti mahānisaṁsan”ti.
“Ko nu kho, bhante, hetu ko paccayo yena midhekaccassa tādisaṁyeva dānaṁ dinnaṁ na mahapphalaṁ hoti na mahānisaṁsaṁ;
verses.english: “Sir, what is the cause, what is the reason for this?”

verses.pali: ko nu kho, bhante, hetu ko paccayo yena midhekaccassa tādisaṁyeva dānaṁ dinnaṁ mahapphalaṁ hoti mahānisaṁsan”ti?
“Idha, sāriputta, ekacco sāpekho dānaṁ deti, patibaddhacitto dānaṁ deti, sannidhipekho dānaṁ deti, ‘imaṁ pecca paribhuñjissāmī’ti dānaṁ deti.
verses.english: “Sāriputta, take the case of a someone who gives a gift as an investment, their mind tied to it, expecting to keep it, thinking ‘I’ll enjoy this in my next life’.

verses.pali: So taṁ dānaṁ deti samaṇassa vā brāhmaṇassa vā annaṁ pānaṁ vatthaṁ yānaṁ mālāgandhavilepanaṁ seyyāvasathapadīpeyyaṁ.
verses.english: They give to ascetics or brahmins such things as food, drink, clothing, vehicles; garlands, fragrance, and makeup; and bed, house, and lighting.

verses.pali: Taṁ kiṁ maññasi, sāriputta, dadeyya idhekacco evarūpaṁ dānan”ti?
verses.english: What do you think, Sāriputta, don’t some people give gifts in this way?”

verses.pali: “Evaṁ, bhante”.
verses.english: “Yes, sir.”

verses.pali: “Tatra, sāriputta, yvāyaṁ sāpekho dānaṁ deti, patibaddhacitto dānaṁ deti, sannidhipekho dānaṁ deti, ‘imaṁ pecca paribhuñjissāmī’ti dānaṁ deti.
verses.english: “Sāriputta, someone who gives a gift as an investment,

verses.pali: So taṁ dānaṁ datvā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā cātumahārājikānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjati.
verses.english: when their body breaks up, after death, is reborn in the company of the gods of the four great kings.

verses.pali: So taṁ kammaṁ khepetvā taṁ iddhiṁ taṁ yasaṁ taṁ ādhipaccaṁ āgāmī hoti āgantā itthattaṁ.
verses.english: When that deed, success, glory, and sovereignty is spent they return to this place.

verses.pali: Idha pana, sāriputta, ekacco na heva kho sāpekho dānaṁ deti, na patibaddhacitto dānaṁ deti, na sannidhipekho dānaṁ deti, na ‘imaṁ pecca paribhuñjissāmī’ti dānaṁ deti;
verses.english: Next, take the case of a someone who gives a gift not as an investment, their mind not tied to it, not expecting to keep it, and not thinking, ‘I’ll enjoy this in my next life’.

verses.pali: api ca kho ‘sāhu dānan’ti dānaṁ deti …pe….
verses.english: But they give a gift thinking, ‘It’s good to give’ …

verses.pali: Napi ‘sāhu dānan’ti dānaṁ deti;
api ca kho ‘dinnapubbaṁ katapubbaṁ pitupitāmahehi na arahāmi porāṇaṁ kulavaṁsaṁ hāpetun’ti dānaṁ deti …pe….
verses.english: They give a gift thinking, ‘Giving was practiced by my father and my father’s father. It would not be right for me to abandon this family tradition.’ …

verses.pali: Napi ‘dinnapubbaṁ katapubbaṁ pitupitāmahehi na arahāmi porāṇaṁ kulavaṁsaṁ hāpetun’ti dānaṁ deti;
api ca kho ‘ahaṁ pacāmi, ime na pacanti, nārahāmi pacanto apacantānaṁ dānaṁ adātun’ti dānaṁ deti …pe….
verses.english: They give a gift thinking, ‘I cook, they don’t. It wouldn’t be right for me to not give to them.’ …

verses.pali: Napi ‘ahaṁ pacāmi, ime na pacanti, nārahāmi pacanto apacantānaṁ dānaṁ adātun’ti dānaṁ deti;
api ca kho ‘yathā tesaṁ pubbakānaṁ isīnaṁ tāni mahāyaññāni ahesuṁ, seyyathidaṁ—
verses.english: They give a gift thinking, ‘The ancient brahmin seers were Aṭṭhaka, Vāmaka, Vāmadeva, Vessāmitta, Yamadaggi, Aṅgīrasa, Bhāradvāja, Vāseṭṭha, Kassapa, and Bhagu.

verses.pali: aṭṭhakassa vāmakassa vāmadevassa vessāmittassa yamadaggino aṅgīrasassa bhāradvājassa vāseṭṭhassa kassapassa bhaguno, evaṁ me ayaṁ dānasaṁvibhāgo bhavissatī’ti dānaṁ deti …pe….
verses.english: Just as they performed great sacrifices, I will share a gift.’ …

verses.pali: Napi ‘yathā tesaṁ pubbakānaṁ isīnaṁ tāni mahāyaññāni ahesuṁ, seyyathidaṁ—
aṭṭhakassa vāmakassa vāmadevassa vessāmittassa yamadaggino aṅgīrasassa bhāradvājassa vāseṭṭhassa kassapassa bhaguno, evaṁ me ayaṁ dānasaṁvibhāgo bhavissatī’ti dānaṁ deti;
api ca kho ‘imaṁ me dānaṁ dadato cittaṁ pasīdati, attamanatā somanassaṁ upajāyatī’ti dānaṁ deti …pe….
verses.english: They give a gift thinking, ‘When giving this gift my mind becomes clear, and I become happy and joyful.’ …

verses.pali: Napi ‘imaṁ me dānaṁ dadato cittaṁ pasīdati, attamanatā somanassaṁ upajāyatī’ti dānaṁ deti;
verses.english: They don’t give a gift thinking, ‘When giving this gift my mind becomes clear, and I become happy and joyful.’

verses.pali: api ca kho cittālaṅkāracittaparikkhāraṁ dānaṁ deti.
verses.english: But they give a gift thinking, ‘This is an adornment and requisite for the mind.’

verses.pali: So taṁ dānaṁ deti samaṇassa vā brāhmaṇassa vā annaṁ pānaṁ vatthaṁ yānaṁ mālāgandhavilepanaṁ seyyāvasathapadīpeyyaṁ.
verses.english: They give to ascetics or brahmins such things as food, drink, clothing, vehicles; garlands, fragrance, and makeup; and bed, house, and lighting.

verses.pali: Taṁ kiṁ maññasi, sāriputta, dadeyya idhekacco evarūpaṁ dānan”ti?
verses.english: What do you think, Sāriputta, don’t some people give gifts in this way?”

verses.pali: “Evaṁ, bhante”.
verses.english: “Yes, sir.”

verses.pali: “Tatra, sāriputta, yvāyaṁ na heva sāpekho dānaṁ deti;
verses.english: “Sāriputta, someone who gives gifts, not for any other reason,

verses.pali: na patibaddhacitto dānaṁ deti;
na sannidhipekho dānaṁ deti;
na ‘imaṁ pecca paribhuñjissāmī’ti dānaṁ deti;
napi ‘sāhu dānan’ti dānaṁ deti;
napi ‘dinnapubbaṁ katapubbaṁ pitupitāmahehi na arahāmi porāṇaṁ kulavaṁsaṁ hāpetun’ti dānaṁ deti;
napi ‘ahaṁ pacāmi, ime na pacanti, nārahāmi pacanto apacantānaṁ dānaṁ adātun’ti dānaṁ deti;
napi ‘yathā tesaṁ pubbakānaṁ isīnaṁ tāni mahāyaññāni ahesuṁ, seyyathidaṁ—
aṭṭhakassa vāmakassa vāmadevassa vessāmittassa yamadaggino aṅgīrasassa bhāradvājassa vāseṭṭhassa kassapassa bhaguno, evaṁ me ayaṁ dānasaṁvibhāgo bhavissatī’ti dānaṁ deti;
napi ‘imaṁ me dānaṁ dadato cittaṁ pasīdati, attamanatā somanassaṁ upajāyatī’ti dānaṁ deti;
api ca kho cittālaṅkāracittaparikkhāraṁ dānaṁ deti.
verses.english: but thinking, ‘This is an adornment and requisite for the mind’,

verses.pali: So taṁ dānaṁ datvā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā brahmakāyikānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjati.
verses.english: when their body breaks up, after death, is reborn among the gods of the Divinity’s host.

verses.pali: So taṁ kammaṁ khepetvā taṁ iddhiṁ taṁ yasaṁ taṁ ādhipaccaṁ anāgāmī hoti anāgantā itthattaṁ.
verses.english: When that deed, success, glory, and sovereignty is spent they are a non-returner; they do not return to this place.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ kho, sāriputta, hetu ayaṁ paccayo yena midhekaccassa tādisaṁyeva dānaṁ dinnaṁ na mahapphalaṁ hoti na mahānisaṁsaṁ.
verses.english: This is the cause, this is the reason why someone gives a gift and it is not very fruitful or beneficial,

verses.pali: Ayaṁ pana, sāriputta, hetu ayaṁ paccayo yena midhekaccassa tādisaṁyeva dānaṁ dinnaṁ mahapphalaṁ hoti mahānisaṁsan”ti.
verses.english: while someone else gives exactly the same gift and it is very fruitful and beneficial.”

verses.pali: Navamaṁ.
